question: Does divisibility of generic sections at the branch fibre bound the entire rational section block of a native quadratic twist?
selection: All 37 native quadratic branch supports retained in rank_jump_branch_block_inputs_v1.json. Their equations are matched exactly to the earlier complete equation-only atlas. The 11 oracle-fitted quartics are excluded. Arithmetic receives only A,B, the 17 published generic section polynomials, labels and branch quadratics. Historical lift-based selection remains retrospective and is not a prospective selector.
method: At primes 3 through 2003 and every simple rational reduction of a branch root, certify irreducibility of the branch cubic when available and collect split-cubic quadratic characters of the 17 generic sections. Skip blocks with a zero section ordinate or bad reduction. Use the joint character rank to upper-bound the branch-specialization kernel. Also certify generic mod-two independence at t=0 using the same prime cap. Verify the original root-curve geometry and exact real component count to bound the global pool. No sections on the twists are sought.
theorem_gate: If every branch fibre has no rational two-torsion over its residue field, all rational twist Kummer classes lie in the original global pool L. A class shared with G is a norm from the quadratic cover, so its specialization is divisible by two at every branch place. Thus rank(twist) <= dim(L)-dim(G)+dim(kernel(G -> product branch Kummer groups)). This bounds every rational scalar twist with the same branch support.
failure: UNKNOWN if generic independence, irreducibility or geometry is not certified within the fixed dictionary. Finite character ranks are lower bounds; corresponding kernel and twist-rank values are upper bounds. Individual specialized curve ranks remain unbounded by this theorem.
